claim_being_audited: That rejecting the vendor was compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved risk at the time of decision, and that the rejection is supportable as a risk-based procurement decision rather than as proof of a reject-level control failure.
specific_concerns: Evidence access is limited to the actor's summary, so the admissible record cannot be independently tested.
The policy threshold requires a material unresolved risk; the summary describes inconsistency, informality, and a follow-up recommendation, but does not clearly establish materiality.
The claim that no admissible record shows the storage-control inconsistency was resolved before decision is not independently supported from the materials provided to this role.
A recommendation for follow-up before approval supports escalation or conditional non-approval, but does not by itself prove that outright rejection was the only compliant outcome.
The actor appropriately avoids claiming a proven control failure, but still may overstate how strongly the record supports rejection versus further diligence.
unsupported_claims: That the unresolved storage-control issue was definitively unresolved at the exact time of rejection.
That the unresolved issue met the policy's materiality threshold for rejection rather than follow-up or escalation.
That the cited record is sufficient, by itself, to defend rejection rather than a pause pending clarification.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying contents of BPROC-049-A through BPROC-049-E, not just their labels and summary.
Provide the dated decision record showing what unresolved issue was relied on when the rejection was made.
Provide any admissible log, memo, or approval note showing whether the storage-control inconsistency was resolved or remained open before the decision.
Provide the procurement policy or rubric, if any, defining when an unresolved diligence issue becomes material enough to justify rejection.
decision_criteria: Policy allows rejection only if admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk.
Questionnaire inconsistencies and quality-process gaps can justify follow-up or escalation, but do not alone prove a reject-level control failure.
Private or unlogged security-review results cannot be cited or indirectly relied on.
Because this role has only the actor summary, claims requiring timing, materiality, or closure status must be treated cautiously unless directly supported.
